claims.claim: Residents are taxed on worldwide income

sources.name: PwC: Montenegro, taxes on personal income
sources.says: Last reviewed 07 August 2026. "Resident individuals are subject to tax on their worldwide income from any source." "Other categories of personal income subject to PIT are taxed at a proportional 15% rate." "A surtax rate of 13% applies in all municipalities, except Podgorica and Cetinje, where the rate is 15%"; its base is the PIT assessed. The page does not say whether the surtax reaches capital income, and describes no newcomer regime.

Capital gains on real estate, shares and securities: "The tax base is the difference between the sale price and the price at which the taxpayer acquired the property"; "The capital gains tax rate is 15%."

claims.claim: Schwab International does not accept Montenegro, which is off its reported list
claims.wording: Schwab International most likely does not accept Montenegro, which is off its reported list

sources.name: Your Tax Base: Charles Schwab for expats
sources.says: Published October 23, 2026. On that day the author ran every entry in Schwab's international account selector through the application: it accepted residents of 51 of 263 countries and regions: Argentina, Australia, Austria, the Bahamas, Belgium, Bermuda, Brazil, the British Virgin Islands, the Cayman Islands, Chile, China, Colombia, Costa Rica, the Czech Republic, Denmark, Ecuador, Finland, Germany, Greece, Guatemala, Hong Kong, Iceland, India, Indonesia, Ireland, Israel, Jersey, Luxembourg, Malaysia, the Marshall Islands, Mexico, the Netherlands, Norway, Panama, Paraguay, Peru, Poland, Portugal, Qatar, Singapore, South Korea, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Taiwan, Thailand, Trinidad and Tobago, Turks and Caicos, the United Arab Emirates, the United Kingdom and Uruguay. Named as not accepted: Canada, Croatia, the Dominican Republic, France, Italy, Japan, Malta, New Zealand, the Philippines, South Africa, Turkey and Vietnam; for the rest the application said "Schwab currently cannot open accounts for residents of your country/region." The test covers new applicants on that day only.

sources.name: Your Tax Base: Charles Schwab for expats
sources.says: Dated October 23, 2026 (country check that day). The United Arab Emirates is on the 51-country accepted list and marked "Yes"; South Africa is marked "No" (the 12 "No" rows: Canada, Croatia, Dominican Republic, France, Italy, Japan, Malta, New Zealand, Philippines, South Africa, Turkey, Vietnam). Montenegro, Albania and Mauritius are in neither list; the article says 200 of the 263 countries and regions in Schwab's selector showed that Schwab "currently cannot open accounts for residents of your country/region". It quotes the Schwab One International terms: "Customers residing within Europe are restricted from using their Available Margin Loan Value to withdraw funds from their account."

claims.note: Montenegro is in neither the accepted 51 nor the 12 marked "No"; the page says 200 of 263 selector entries showed Schwab cannot open accounts there, which supports "most likely". Lending score stays 3 ("IBKR only"). Montenegro is in Europe, so Schwab's reported "residing within Europe" margin clause would bar cash-out even if Schwab accepted residents; that is the London/Zurich reading (plan decision 2026-11-15), and it gives 3 either way, since 4 needs Schwab "outside Europe" and 2 needs IBKR itself in doubt or EU residence.

sources.says: Retail clients are "not permitted to trade ETFs or other products that do not have a valid KID"; many non-EU ETFs have none. Can a retail client buy US ETFs? also: hedge added: the flat "do not apply" became "should not apply, though which IBKR entity carries the account is unconfirmed" (as Turkey's tr-lending-priips-not-applicable)

claims.claim: Temporary residence by owning real estate with a Tax Authority-assessed value of at least €150,000, since January 2026, with older permits grandfathered

sources.name: BDK Advokati: Montenegro adopts amendments to the Foreigners Act
sources.says: The amendments "entered into force on 17 January 2026". Applicants for temporary residence on real estate must "submit evidence that their real estate is worth at least EUR 150,000", the value determined "based on the decision of the Tax Authority on transfer tax"; permits issued before that date "can be extended without demonstrating the value of the real estate".

sources.name: NT Realty: Montenegro property residency rules 2026
sources.says: Published January 2026, "updated in May 2026". Law in force 17 January 2026; €150,000 threshold on the official tax valuation; holders before that date "may renew without demonstrating the new €150,000 threshold". Per official guidance as the article describes it, property-based temporary residence "does not count toward the five-year qualifying period for permanent residence."

claims.claim: The permit also needs means of subsistence and health insurance

Threshold "€150,000" on the tax-assessed value.

claims.note: Secondary page (2026); the Ministry of Interior's pages were not found by search, and gov.me refused the connection.
